scope: Sample-level verification of the immutable Parquet fallback against rows-API content.

comparison.method: Compare every cached raw row field with m0_parquet.parquet_page(...), reading all Parquet columns; compare canonical subset content digests.
Direct equality of the complete rows-API raw row and all-column immutable Parquet raw row.
Direct equality of the complete rows-API raw row and all-column immutable Parquet raw row.

canonical_digest_format: sha256-canonical-json-v1: sort rows by row_idx; JSON encode every raw row including row_idx with sorted keys, UTF-8, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(comma,colon), allow_nan=False; hash each JSON record followed by LF.
offline_verification: All five test_parquet_fetch tests passed, including global indices across row groups/shards, bounded HTTP ranges, unchanged source revision and expected split length.
Additional in-memory all-column comparison preserved every field of nested/null records exactly across row-group boundaries.
limitations: Source commits and Parquet conversion commits are separately pinned and verified. Matching current source SHA and representative row content does not establish a cryptographic conversion-to-source association.
HC3 comparison covers all 1,315 unique rows retained from the 14 original API blocks, not the complete source corpus.
Wiki and RAID comparisons cover only row 0 of each converted split; no full-corpus equality claim is made.
RAID uses the 2,270,000-row available partial conversion, not an asserted full source split.
The rows API can truncate large cells. New fetch blocks reject nonempty truncated_cells; this audit found no existing HC3 API-cache mismatch.
Final training sample coverage, grouping, balance, split independence and fitted-model validation are recorded separately from this transport audit.
No source dataset, fetch cache or model artifact was modified by these verification comparisons.
